proof_attempt_summary: Five D0 solve rounds and two distinct maximality repairs produced an analytic atom-onset reduction and executed external numerical certificates, including a 91,340-box homogeneous cover reporting 63.38215 < H_star <= 63.42. D0.5 graded the disclosed partial package incremental below the field floor and retained kernel_substituted plus three certificate-not-discharged findings: external finite covers, normal-enclosure arrays, scripts and checker receipts could not be reconstructed from declared core dependencies. No Lean was produced and no formal-verification claim is made; the sharp heterogeneous envelope, least-favorable regimes and global attaining kernel require a dedicated simultaneous primal-dual numerical implementation and independently reconstructible certificate payloads.
tldr: At the stipulated nonemployment atom, the original-record causal regret converges to a positive finite Gaussian minimax value, attained by a total rule learning the unknown tails and propensities. The sharp global number remains unevaluated. This round improves the executed homogeneous envelope certificate to \(63.38215<H_\star\le63.42\), uniformly over all homogeneous coefficients, exponents and propensities, and proves that the supplied endpoint prior's specified Bayes kernel is not minimax. The required global \(.01\)-width certificate, least-favorable nuisance set and heterogeneous-versus-homogeneous comparison remain open.
gap: Existing lower-tail policy theory and generic Gaussian treatment-choice theory do not evaluate the stipulated full-record atom-onset minimax experiment with unknown positive-tail attachment.
fill: The proposal binds the entire four-policy decision game, certified nuisance-envelope evaluation, full likelihood converse, and uniform observable attainment into one result. The unresolved least-favorable geometry remains an explicit research question. Radius and second-order-power sensitivity make the pilot and sharp-transfer dependence explicit; cell-specific slopes receive a separate welfare decomposition.
